fields.features_heading: What a Coach Knows Before the First Call
fields.features_subheading: Emergent builds a health coaching intake form around the habit a client wants to change and the history a coach should know.
fields.feature_1:
Importance and confidence, rated apart

Ask the client to name one habit, then rate how important it is and how confident they feel about it, each from 1 to 10. Both scores sit side by side on the coach's prep sheet.
fields.feature_2:
Sections for the areas a client picks

A client who picks sleep gets questions on bedtime, wake time, and coffee. One who picks stress gets questions on workload, and nobody scrolls past a section that does not apply.
fields.feature_3:
A question about care already under way

Ask whether a doctor is treating any condition and, if so, for the doctor's name. The coach knows who else is involved before agreeing on a goal that touches food or exercise.
fields.feature_4:
A coaching agreement signed on the form

Close the intake with your coaching agreement, session terms included, and a typed or drawn signature. Each signature is saved with its date next to the answers that came with it.
fields.feature_5:
An email or Slack alert for each new intake

Each submitted intake sends the coach an email or a Slack message that a new intake is ready, with the client's name. The full answers stay on the prep sheet inside the app.
fields.feature_6:
Code that moves to your own GitHub

On paid plans, export the code for the intake and the prep sheet to your GitHub repository. A developer can then host it on your own servers and keep building on it from there.

fields.tab_content_1:
On the prep sheet, a 5-point gap comes first

Thaddea Ruskin coaches clients by video at Pinecrown Health Coaching. Her intake asks each new client to name one habit and rate its importance and their confidence from 1 to 10. Evander Pyle rates walking after dinner 9 and 4. A gap of 5 points or more puts the habit first on her prep sheet, and his call opens there.
fields.tab_content_2:
Every focus area routes to its own coach

Coldbrook Haulage offers health coaching to its drivers through Sorrelwood Coaching Group. Each employee enrolls on one intake and picks a focus area: sleep, stress, or eating. Each area goes to its own coach. HR sees 46 enrollments by area, 14 for sleep, 19 for stress, and 13 for eating, and none of the answers.
fields.tab_content_3:
Coffees after 2 pm, next to 5 hours 45 minutes in bed

Cressida Wilmot coaches poor sleepers at Driftmoor Sleep Coaching. Her intake asks for a workday bedtime, a wake time, and coffees after 2 pm. Leander Banerjee enters 12:30 am, 6:15 am, and 2. The form works out 5 hours 45 minutes in bed and puts that total on her prep sheet beside his coffee count.
fields.tab_content_4:
When two Sundays pass with no check-in, an email goes out

Every Sunday, clients of Linfield Health Coaching get a short check-in on their habit. Beatrix Fitzalan skipped it on Oct 18 and again on Oct 25. On Monday, Arvid Kincaid got an email saying she had missed 2 in a row, and nothing more. Her earlier answers stay in the app, where he reads them before he calls.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Health Coaching Intake Form
fields.howto_description: Plan the questions, the ratings, and the doctor check for a health coaching intake form, then build it with Emergent in seven steps.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 List the changes clients ask for
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Show the sleep section only for sleep
fields.howto_step_1_des: Write down the changes your last 20 clients wanted to make, such as sleeping longer or walking more after work. Group them into a short list of focus areas. Each area becomes one choice on the form, with its own section of questions.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Ask for one habit and two ratings on it, importance and confidence, each from 1 to 10. Keep them as two questions rather than one combined score. The prep sheet needs both numbers to show the gap between them.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Set the sleep questions to appear only when a client picks sleep. Keep each section to 5 or 6 questions. Times, counts, and ratings compare cleanly at a later check-in, and open text does not.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Put the question about current medical care, and the doctor's name, ahead of any goal question. The NBHWC states that coaches do not prescribe medications or provide medical advice. A yes keeps that doctor in view for any goal on food or exercise.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Paste your coaching agreement in as the last page, with session length, the rescheduling policy, and what coaching does not cover. Place the signature after the answers. The client then reads the terms with the rest of the intake finished.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Put the focus areas, the two ratings, the section rules, and who gets the alert into one prompt. Emergent builds the intake, the database behind it, and the coach's prep sheet. Change any question later by asking in plain English.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Submit one test intake with a 5-point gap, one that picks sleep, and one that answers yes to the doctor question. Check that the coach's alert says only that an intake is ready, and that every answer lands on the prep sheet.

faq_plan.q: What is a health coaching intake form?
faq_plan.a: A health coaching intake form is the questionnaire a new client fills in before the first coaching session. It records the habit they want to change, how ready they feel to change it, and any care a doctor already provides. The coach reads it to help the client set a first goal.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a health coaching intake form?
faq_plan.a: Decide on the focus areas, the readiness ratings, and who hears about each new intake. Describe all of it in one prompt to Emergent's AI form builder, which builds the form, the database behind it, and a prep sheet for the coach. Then submit a made-up client to check each section.

faq_plan.q: What questions should a health coaching intake form ask?
faq_plan.a: Start with contact details and the reason the client came. Ask for one habit to change, rated for importance and confidence, then short sections on sleep, stress, and eating that open only when chosen. Add the medical care question, then close with the coaching agreement. Emergent builds those sections from a plain-English description.

faq_plan.q: Can a life coach use a health coaching intake form?
faq_plan.a: Partly. The importance and confidence ratings carry over to any coaching goal, but the sleep, stress, and eating sections and the medical care question belong to health coaching. For goals about work, money, or relationships, start from a life coaching intake form instead.

faq_plan.q: How do you measure readiness to change on a health coaching intake form?
faq_plan.a: Use rulers. The confidence ruler was first described by Bill Miller and Stephen Rollnick, the founders of motivational interviewing. Ask how confident the client feels about one change on a scale of 1 to 10, and ask how important it is on the same scale. Repeat both ratings at a later check-in to see whether confidence has moved.

faq_plan.q: How should a health coaching intake form handle medical history?
faq_plan.a: Keep it to one question: is a doctor treating the client for anything right now, and if so, who? Leave diagnoses and medication lists off the form. The NBHWC describes coaches as helping clients set goals and commit to action steps, and the doctor's name is enough for the coach to know who else is involved.

faq_plan.q: What does a health coaching intake form ask that other client intakes skip?
faq_plan.a: It asks about the person rather than a project. An accounting client intake form gathers entity details and tax documents. A health coaching intake asks which habit the client wants to change, how confident they are about it, and how they sleep and handle stress. Its answers set a first goal instead of a scope of work.

faq_plan.q: How are health coaching intake forms stored after a client submits them?
faq_plan.a: In a database. Emergent builds the form on a database you own, and each intake is a record the coach opens from the prep sheet. The email or Slack alert to the coach carries the client's name only, and the answers stay in the app.

faq_plan.q: Can a health coaching intake form ask one question at a time?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Emergent can build it as a conversational flow with one question per screen. Put the importance and confidence ratings on separate screens, and give each a short label at both ends of the scale, such as not at all and completely.

faq_plan.q: Should a health coaching intake form include fitness tests?
faq_plan.a: No. An intake records what the client reports from home, such as hours in bed or coffees after 2 pm. Save measured tests, such as push-ups or a timed walk, for a fitness assessment form at the first session.

plan.angle: Searches for a health coaching intake form return printable questionnaires that list every lifestyle topic and stop there.
